newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Explosion rocks ammo dump in south Albania.
newsitem.headline: Explosion rocks ammo dump in south Albania.

text.p: An explosion rocked an ammunition dump in southern Albania on Thursday and 14 people were taken to hospital with burns, military officials and doctors said.
There was no immediate word if anyone was killed in the blast.

Officials said explosions at the dump, some some 18 kms (10 miles) north of Gjirokaster, Albania's southernmost town, was still going on. They spoke of a "big, dynamite explosion" in underground tunnels and in depots on the surface.

Ammunition dumps all over Albania were looted during rioting and lawlessness which swept the country after thousands lost their life savings in collapsed investment schemes last February. Two weeks ago a dump exploded in northern Albania, killing 27 people.
Gjirokaster hospital director Hodo Cela said 14 people had been brought in with burns. Six were transferred to a hospital in Greece.
Local residents said the army was removing ammunition, powder and shells from the warehouses when the blast took place but there was no immediate explanation of exactly what caused the blasts.
